articles.title: Why Do Stock Prices Move? 股价为什么会波动？

paras.en: A stock price is simply the price buyers and sellers agree on at a moment. When more people want to buy than to sell, the price goes up. When more people want to sell, it goes down.
paras.zh: 股价就是买卖双方在某一时刻达成的价格。当想买的人多于想卖的人，价格就上涨；当想卖的人更多，价格就下跌。

paras.en: Behind the buying and selling are expectations. If investors believe a company will earn more in the future, they are willing to pay more for its shares today. Bad news about profits can push the price down quickly.
paras.zh: 买卖的背后是预期。如果投资者相信一家公司未来能赚更多钱，他们今天就愿意为它的股票付更高的价格。而盈利方面的坏消息会让股价迅速下跌。

paras.en: Emotions matter too. Fear can make a whole market fall at once, and greed can lift prices far above what a business is really worth. Learning to notice these emotions — in the market and in yourself — is the first step of investing.
paras.zh: 情绪同样重要。恐惧可以让整个市场同时下跌，贪婪可以把价格抬到远超企业真实价值的水平。学会觉察这些情绪——市场中的和你自己的——是投资的第一步。

notes: agree on sth. 固定搭配：就某事达成一致，介词用 on
be willing to do 愿意做某事——写作口语双料高频
far above 远高于；反义 far below 远低于
in the market and in yourself：介词短语并列，emphasis 结构收尾有力

articles.title: Bull and Bear Markets 牛市与熊市

paras.en: A bull market is a long period in which prices keep rising and people feel confident. A bear market is the opposite: prices fall, often by twenty percent or more, and pessimism spreads.
paras.zh: 牛市是价格持续上涨、人们充满信心的漫长时期。熊市则相反：价格下跌，跌幅常常达到百分之二十以上，悲观情绪蔓延。

paras.en: No one can predict exactly when a bull becomes a bear. But history shows one thing clearly: markets have always recovered from every bear market so far, though it can take months or years.
paras.zh: 没有人能精确预测牛市何时变成熊市。但历史清楚地表明一件事：到目前为止，市场总能从每一次熊市中恢复过来，尽管这可能需要数月甚至数年。

paras.en: For a beginner, the lesson is simple. In a bull market, stay humble and avoid chasing prices. In a bear market, stay patient — cheap prices are the friend of the long-term buyer.
paras.zh: 对初学者来说，教训很简单。牛市里保持谦逊，不要追涨；熊市里保持耐心——便宜的价格是长期买入者的朋友。

notes: in which prices keep rising：介词 + which 的定语从句，正式书面句式
so far 到目前为止——现在完成时的标志性时间状语
avoid doing sth.：avoid 后接动名词，不说 avoid to do
破折号 — 引出补充解释，比逗号更有强调感

articles.title: Compound Interest: The Eighth Wonder 复利：第八大奇迹

paras.en: Compound interest means your money earns returns, and then those returns earn returns too. A small sum, given enough time, can grow far beyond your intuition.
paras.zh: 复利是指你的钱产生收益，而这些收益又继续产生收益。一笔小钱，只要时间够长，可以增长到远超直觉的程度。

paras.en: Suppose you invest 10,000 yuan at an 8% yearly return. In 10 years it becomes about 21,600; in 30 years, about 100,600. The last ten years add more than the first twenty combined.
paras.zh: 假设你以每年 8% 的收益投资一万元。十年后它变成约 21,600 元；三十年后约 100,600 元。最后十年增加的部分，超过了前二十年的总和。

paras.en: The same rule applies to learning. Twenty English words a day feels small, but a year of consistency is more than seven thousand words. Time multiplies small daily actions — this is the real logic behind this app.
paras.zh: 同样的规律也适用于学习。每天二十个单词看起来很少，但坚持一年就是七千多个。时间会放大微小的日常行动——这正是这个 APP 背后的真正逻辑。

notes: given enough time = if given enough time，条件句的省略式（写作加分）
Suppose (that)… 假设……，引出演算例子，比 if 更正式
apply to 适用于——the rule applies to learning 规律适用于学习
combined 作后置定语：the first twenty combined 前两者之和

articles.title: What Is a P/E Ratio? 市盈率是什么？

paras.en: The P/E ratio, or price-to-earnings ratio, is the price of a stock divided by its earnings per share. In plain words, it tells you how many years it would take to earn back your investment, assuming profits stay the same.
paras.zh: 市盈率（P/E）等于股价除以每股盈利。用大白话说：假设利润不变，它告诉你需要几年才能赚回你的投资。

paras.en: A high P/E often means investors expect fast growth. A low P/E may signal a boring but stable business — or a company in trouble. The number alone never tells the whole story.
paras.zh: 高市盈率往往意味着投资者期待快速增长。低市盈率可能代表一门无聊但稳定的生意——也可能是一家陷入麻烦的公司。单看数字永远讲不出全部真相。

paras.en: Smart investors compare the P/E with the company's own history and with other companies in the same industry. A ratio means something only in context.
paras.zh: 聪明的投资者会把市盈率和公司自身的历史比、和同行业的公司比。任何比率只有在对比中才有意义。

notes: price-to-earnings：数字复合形容词用连字符合成，如 a 10-year plan
assuming profits stay the same = if we assume…，分词引出前提
signal 作动词=预示/表明，财经新闻高频
in context 在具体背景下——对比才有意义

articles.title: Don't Bet the Farm 仓位管理：别押上全部家当

paras.en: Betting the farm means risking everything on one move. In investing, it happens when someone puts most of their money into a single stock, hoping to get rich quickly.
paras.zh: 『押上农场』就是孤注一掷。在投资中，它发生在一个人把大部分钱押进一只股票、幻想快速暴富的时候。

paras.en: Professional money managers follow a simple rule: no single position should be large enough to destroy the whole portfolio. If one company fails, the rest can still carry you forward.
paras.zh: 职业基金经理遵守一条简单规则：任何单一持仓都不应大到足以摧毁整个组合。就算一家公司倒下，其余部分仍能带你继续前行。

paras.en: The math is cruel: a 50% loss needs a 100% gain just to break even. Protecting your capital is not cowardice — it is the first skill of surviving the market.
paras.zh: 数学很残酷：亏损 50%，需要盈利 100% 才能回本。保护本金不是怯懦——它是你在市场里活下来的第一项技能。

notes: bet the farm 习语：孤注一掷（把农场都押上）
large enough to…：enough to do 足以……的经典结构
break even 固定表达：不赚不亏、打平
冒号 + 解释：The math is cruel: … 口语演讲皆可用的强调句式
